scenes.title: Keygen
scenes.subtitle: Build guide
say: This is Keygen: a wireless, split, ergonomic keyboard, with sixty-six keys, a rotary encoder and an OLED screen on each half, and a light under every key.
Let's build one, step by step, from bare boards to a finished, tented keyboard.

scenes.heading: Each half is a stack
say: Each half is a stack.
A printed bottom shell holds the battery and a layer of foam.
Above it, the PCB, with almost every part on its underside.
A clear polycarbonate plate rests on brass standoffs, with foam taped under it.
The switches clip into the plate, and plug into hotswap sockets on the PCB.
A printed top frame holds the OLED and the encoder, and screws down over everything.
Foam gaskets between the shell and the frame let the whole typing surface float.

scenes.heading: What goes where
steps: Find it on the map first
say: Everything goes on the back of the board, except the switches and the OLED header.
The right half mirrors the left. Left parts are numbered in the one-hundreds, right parts in the two-hundreds: Q101 on the left is Q201 on the right.
Find each part on its assembly map before you solder it.

scenes.heading: Electronics, both halves
say: For both halves, you need two PCBs, two nRF52840 SuperMini controllers, sixty-six reverse-mount LEDs, sixty-eight diodes, and sixty-six hotswap sockets.
Plus a small power section per half, two encoders, two OLEDs, and two LiPo pouches with protection boards.

scenes.heading: Switches, case and hardware
say: Sixty-six Akko Lavender Purple switches, blank DSA keycaps, and two aluminium knobs.
A polycarbonate plate, a PETG case, Poron and EVA foam, M2 hardware, feet, and the optional magnetic wedges.

scenes.heading: Tools
say: For tools: a temperature-controlled iron with a fine tip, flux, wick, fine tweezers, a multimeter, calipers and a magnifier.

scenes.heading: The plan
details: Fit test. Order PCBs and every part
Measure. Cut plates and plate foam
Measure. Print case, cut case foam
say: Some parts are made to fit others, so the order matters.
On day one, print the fit test and order everything.
When the OLEDs arrive, measure one, then cut the plates and the plate foam.
When the sockets and pins are in too, measure them, then print the case and cut its foam.
Meanwhile, solder and test both boards.
Then the OLED lead, the standoffs and the switch pads,
the plate and switches,
and finally, the case.

scenes.heading: Fit test and PCBs
say: Print the fit test at actual size, and check that its ruler measures exactly one hundred millimetres. Rest your hands on it to check the thumb keys and the knob.
Then order the PCBs: two orders of five, one per half, with black solder mask.

scenes.heading: When the parts arrive
say: When the parts arrive, check that the OLED's pins read GND, VCC, SCL, SDA. Modules with GND and VCC swapped are no good.
Each battery needs a protection board, and the connector must be the side-entry type.
Dry-fit the encoder and knob on the test coupon, before cutting the shaft by one millimetre.

scenes.heading: Plates, foam and case
say: Have both plates CNC-routed from one-and-a-half millimetre clear polycarbonate. Not laser-cut.
Cut the foam from its four files: two-millimetre EVA for the plates, five-millimetre for the case floors.
Print the shells and frames in PETG, at ninety percent infill, without supports. The fits are close, so calibrate the printer first.

note.text: Fits are close: 1.0 mm plate to wall, 0.5 mm round each gasket tab.

scenes.heading: Inspect, then solder
say: Before soldering, check the bare board for clean LED cut-outs, and use the meter to check that the power rails aren't shorted to ground.
Every small surface-mount part goes on the same way: tin one pad, place the part and reheat it, solder the rest, then touch up the first.

warning.text: Keep the battery unplugged whenever you solder.

scenes.heading: Battery switch
say: Start on the back, beside the controller: the AO3401A MOSFET at Q101,
and the one-megohm resistor R101, just below it.

scenes.heading: LED boost converter
say: Next, the LED boost. U102 is a TPS61023, with half-millimetre pins: flux the pads, line up pin one, touch each pad, and check for bridges.
Then the inductor L101, and the capacitors C101, C104 and C103.
And the feedback divider, R102 and R104, with the pull-down R103.

warning.text: Ceramic capacitors carry no marking. Keep each value in its labelled bag.

scenes.heading: LED data buffer
steps: C105 10 µF, by the last LED
say: The data buffer, U103, goes beside the first LED, with C102 and R105.
C105 goes beside the last LED.
The small footprints beside each LED stay empty.

scenes.heading: Connector, reset, power switch
steps: SW190  slide switch, knob over the edge
say: The battery connector, BT101,
the reset button, SW191,
and the slide switch, SW190, its knob out over the top edge, are through-hole: place them on the back, solder them on the front, and trim flush.

scenes.heading: Controller
steps: Chip up, USB-C at the top edge
say: Before fitting the controller, check that VCC reads three point three volts on USB, and bridge its BOOST link for faster charging.
Push the socket strips into the footprint, the machined pins into the sockets, and lay the controller on top.
Chip side up, away from the PCB, with the USB-C at the top edge.
Solder the pins to the controller, then the sockets on the front.

warning.text: Seated chip-side down, the pinout is mirrored and the battery lands on a GPIO.

scenes.heading: Bring-up
say: Now bring the half up, before any LED goes on. Flash the firmware, and check that it shows up over USB.
Confirm the red battery wire lands on the plus pad.
With the LED test build, the LED rail at C101 should read between four point eight three and five point oh eight volts.
And the charge current should be about three hundred milliamps.

warning.text: JST-PH packs come wired both ways round. Check the polarity every time.

scenes.heading: LEDs
steps: In order, six at a time
say: The thirty-three LEDs mount upside down on the back, shining through their cut-outs.
The cut corner marks ground, on pad one. Use three hundred and twenty degrees, and plenty of flux.
Solder them in number order, six or so at a time,
and test as you go: one bad joint darkens every LED after it.

scenes.heading: Diodes and hotswap sockets
say: Then the diodes, D101 to D134, each with its band towards pad one.
And the thirty-three hotswap sockets: held flat, with plenty of solder.

scenes.heading: Encoder lead and matrix test
steps: Test every key and the encoder
say: Solder a five-pin right-angle header into J102, beside the encoder opening, pointing away from the thumb keys.
Make a five-wire lead, a hundred millimetres long, to the encoder's A, C, B, S1 and S2 pins, and mark pin one.
Plug it in, short each socket with tweezers to test every key, then turn and press the encoder.

scenes.heading: OLED header and lead
say: The last soldering: a four-pin right-angle header in J101, from the front.
Make a four-wire lead, forty-five millimetres long, in GND, VCC, SCL, SDA order, soldered to the module from its back.
Plug it in and power up: the status screen should appear.

warning.text: A module with GND and VCC swapped is powered backwards.

scenes.heading: Standoffs
say: Five standoffs per half: a half-millimetre shim, an M2 standoff, and a screw driven up from the back. Snug, not hard.
Together, they make the three-and-a-half millimetre gap between the PCB and the plate.

scenes.heading: Switch pads
steps: On the PCB, never the plate
say: Then a Poron ring round each switch position, on the PCB, never on the plate.
Clean the board, line each ring's notches up with the switch clips, and press it down.
Where a ring meets a standoff's shim, snip that bite out.

warning.text: No more soldering once the rings are on: a hot iron melts them.

scenes.heading: Plate foam and plate
steps: 2 mm EVA taped under the plate
say: Tape the plate foam under the plate with thin tissue tape, keeping the latch notches clear.
Then rest the plate on the standoffs. The switches will hold it.
That leaves half a millimetre of Poron, a millimetre of air, and two of EVA.

scenes.heading: Switches
say: Dry-fit one switch first.
Then press each one through the plate into its socket, supporting the PCB behind it. The tall thumb switches turn ninety degrees.
While you can still reach the battery lead, check the sleep current: tens to low hundreds of microamps.

scenes.heading: Inserts, battery, case foam
steps: 8 heat-set inserts in the top frame
say: Press the eight heat-set inserts into the top frame's underside, flush with the surface.
Tape the battery into its bay, with the lead towards the connector.
And lay the case foam on the floor, round the battery.

warning.text: Never press, fold or puncture the pouch.

scenes.heading: Encoder in the top frame
steps: Press: the frame must not flex
say: The encoder mounts in the top frame: its bushing through the boss, terminals A, C and B towards the thumbs.
Washer and M7 nut on top, only just tight: the nut can crush PETG.
Press the shaft hard: the frame shouldn't flex.

scenes.heading: Close the case
steps: OLED on its pegs, frame on
say: Put a gasket strip on each of the eight ledges, and plug in the battery with a loose loop.
Plug in the encoder lead, lower the plate and PCB onto the gaskets, and add a second gasket on each tab.
Fix the OLED on the frame's four pegs, plug it in, and lower the frame.
Drive the eight screws up through the floor, evenly, and only snug, so the gaskets stay soft.

scenes.heading: Keycaps, knob and final test
say: Fit the keycaps, the tall thumb caps turned ninety degrees, and push on the knobs.
Turn both halves on together to pair them, then pair your computer on profile one.
And test every key, on every layer.

scenes.heading: Feet and tenting
say: Stick four feet on each floor, and press the steel disc into its pocket.
For tenting, glue four magnets into each wedge: they hold the disc, at thirteen degrees.

scenes.heading: Flashing
say: To flash firmware, plug the half in over USB-C,
double-press reset, through the pinhole in the case,
and copy the UF2 file onto the NICENANO drive.
If the halves won't pair, flash settings reset to both.

scenes.heading: Troubleshooting
say: If a key is dead, check its switch, its diode and its socket. If the LEDs go dark from one point on, check the first dark LED, or the one before it.
And watch for the classics: a reversed diode or battery, the controller upside down, bent pins, and cold joints.
And that's Keygen: built, flashed and tented.
Every file, every part and the full written guide are in the repository.
